intro.title: The Great Convergence — Why AI Software Development, Why Now
intro.note: Opening teaching map for Matt Weber. “The Great Convergence” is Matt's framing for the forces changing software development: capable models, agent harnesses, faster development cadence, and organizations reclaiming software that fits how they actually work.

children.title: Welcome — I am Matt Weber
Senior software developer for a few decades
children.note: Establish experience without turning the introduction into a résumé. The useful point is that this perspective comes from living through several generations of software practice.

children.title: Recent work — Angular frontends and C# backends
Then I discovered AI software development
children.note: Describe this as a change in the way software is conceived, delegated, built, tested, and maintained—not merely a faster autocomplete.

children.title: I built open-source platform tools to exercise what I was learning
children.note: The tools were a laboratory: build real systems, expose weak assumptions, and turn discoveries into repeatable practices.

children.title: Now I am fascinated by how to teach it
Contact — golfergeek@gmail.com
The opening premise
Software was the natural first proving ground for foundation models
children.note: Code offers enormous training material, rapid feedback, executable tests, compilers, linters, and observable outputs. It is more verifiable than many knowledge-work domains, although production software is never perfectly deterministic.

children.title: Code is unusually testable—not magically simple
children.note: A build can pass or fail and a test can pass or fail. Requirements, architecture, security, usability, and business fit still require judgment. This distinction keeps the argument credible.

children.title: The early road became visible very quickly
The road from suggestion to agency
1 — Code completion
Predict the next line or block
The developer remains the primary operator
Useful acceleration, but still centered on typing code
2 — Code generation
Describe a function, test, component, or application slice
The model produces larger coherent units of work
The bottleneck starts moving from typing to definition and review
3 — Agent harnesses
children.note: Claude Code and the growing family of IDE, CLI, plugin, and agent-first environments made the model part of an operating loop.

children.title: Prompt — the immediate request
Context — repository, instructions, history, and retrieved knowledge
Tools — files, terminal, browser, APIs, databases, and other agents
LLM — reasoning and generation inside the loop
Harness — assembles the loop, permissions, state, and interface
Agent — pursues an outcome, observes evidence, and iterates
What changed when the harness arrived
The unit of work became an outcome, not a completion
children.note: The developer can ask for a researched, implemented, tested, and explained change rather than accepting one suggestion at a time.

children.title: Context became an engineering discipline
What must the agent know?
What should remain durable project or organizational memory?
What belongs in code, documentation, a skill, an agent, or the current task?
Tools turned language into action
Evidence allowed the loop to continue
Build, lint, test, run, inspect, challenge, and revise
Longer model runs matter only when feedback remains trustworthy
Every week improves some part of the system
Models become more capable
Context windows and usable working memory grow
Harnesses and IDEs improve orchestration and visibility
Agents work longer and recover from more failures
The four forces converging
1 — Capable foundation models
children.note: Models can understand and produce increasingly large, connected portions of a software system.

children.title: 2 — Operational harnesses
children.note: IDEs, CLIs, plugins, agent views, tools, context, skills, and sub-agents turn model capability into repeatable work.

children.title: 3 — Radical development cadence
children.note: Cadence means the rate at which a team can move from intention to evidence and then safely begin the next iteration.

children.title: 4 — Companies need software that fits
SaaS gives broad capability but rarely matches every workflow
Spreadsheets and internal stopgaps expose the remaining gaps
AI changes the build-versus-buy boundary
Organizations can selectively reclaim differentiating software
Cadence changes the developer's job
From writing every line to managing contracts
children.note: The developer increasingly defines outcomes, boundaries, interfaces, invariants, evidence, and authority. “Contract manager” is a useful metaphor, but technical judgment and accountability stay with the developer.

children.title: One developer can coordinate parallel work
Multiple sub-agents on one bounded issue
Multiple tasks progressing across one codebase
Multiple codebases open in one working environment
Humans integrate decisions, conflicts, and proof
Capable agents can implement many professional tasks
children.note: Avoid the universal claim that an agent is simply “as good as most coders.” Performance varies by task, context, tools, model, and verification. The important change is useful implementation capacity under strong supervision.

children.title: The scarce work moves
Choosing the right problem
Defining boundaries and acceptance criteria
Supplying trustworthy context
Reviewing architecture, security, and product fit
Verifying evidence and retaining organizational learning
The rhythm of software development changes
Specifications become living instruments
children.note: Teams still need shared intent. The difference is that they can test an interpretation quickly, inspect working software, and revise the specification with evidence.

children.title: Fewer meetings devoted only to expensive handoffs
More conversations about decisions, risks, and tradeoffs
Shorter loop — define → delegate → inspect → learn → repeat
Rapid iteration replaces the fantasy of perfect first-pass requirements
Taking back the software process
Not “replace every SaaS product”
children.note: Buy commodity capability when it fits. Build where workflow, integration, data, control, or differentiation makes ownership worthwhile.

children.title: Own the gaps that matter
Turn spreadsheet stopgaps into intentional systems
Keep code, decisions, skills, agents, and governance together
Make organizational learning compound in the repository
The promise and the warning
Speed amplifies good definition—and bad assumptions
Parallel agents amplify capacity—and coordination risk
Large context helps—but does not guarantee understanding
Green tests are evidence—not proof of product value or safety
Governance must move at the new cadence
The winning capability is a trustworthy development system
What this program teaches
Define well
Build fast
Verify hard
Understand before changing
Coordinate tools, agents, and counterparties
Govern reusable skills and agents
Evaluate models against your work
Maintain an agent-queryable organizational AI program
Opening discussion
Where has SaaS forced your process to fit the tool?
Which spreadsheet or internal stopgap reveals an ownable gap?
Where is typing code still your real bottleneck?
What would faster cadence change about your meetings and handoffs?
Which decisions must never be delegated without human authority?
What evidence would make you trust an agent-produced change?
The Great Convergence
children.note: Capable models + operational harnesses + radically faster cadence + the need for software that fits. The opportunity is not just to generate more code. It is to redesign how an organization decides, builds, verifies, learns, and owns software.

children.title: This is not the end of software development
It is a new operating model for software development
The rest of the week is about learning to operate it responsibly

Instructor intent
AI makes a narrow product slice economically possible
Real means identity, protected routes, persisted data, and isolation
The browser may ask; server and database must decide

SaaS bargain and the newly ownable misfit
Vibe coding versus vibe engineering
Auth/data chain: signup → sign in → protect → persist → isolate

Data contract before UI
Lab
Challenge intention, PRD, and plan

Per-user records and server-side authorization

Instructor intent
Generation is cheap; comprehension and review are scarce
Scanners find, fixers fix—never the same step
Standards compound when review findings become future gates
Before
Phase 01 app runs from a known commit
Prepare real, ambiguous, and false-positive findings
Show CI/protected-branch expectations
Teach
Build/test, architecture, and severity are different failure classes
Finding confidence is not evidence
Scanner → fixer; monitor → hardener; commit gate → PR evaluator
Observability lives in diffs, checks, and review records
Lab
Scan and prioritize
Challenge or reject at least one finding
Fix approved issues with regression tests
Monitor and harden an architecture boundary
Run commit gate and independent PR evaluation
Verify affected flow in running software
Close
Promote one repeated lesson into test, rule, skill, or program doc
Explain where human judgment entered
Next: understand unfamiliar code before changing it
Instructor intent
AI can accelerate comprehension; evidence must remain visible
Observe → infer → question; confidence is not evidence
Every investigation should improve repository memory
Before
Authorized sanitized repository or curriculum target
No production secrets or uncontrolled writes
Choose team or individual investigation mode
Teach
Ingest, map, security scan, git story, improve, deep dive
Current code says what; history often explains why
Facts, hypotheses, contradictions, and unknowns
Memory maturity: observation → explanation → expectation → enforcement
Lab
Frame questions and predict likely findings
Trace entry points, data flow, boundaries, tests, and operations
Reconcile parallel reports into one story
Produce research packet with evidence and uncertainty
Make only a bounded improvement with explicit verification
Close
Report one fact, hypothesis, risk, non-change, and improved guardrail
Promote durable findings no farther than evidence earns
Next: independent agents and company-facing protocols

Surface, identity, authority, policy
Evidence, attention, intervention, accountability
Timeout, cancellation, revocation, dispute, and audit
